newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish fx bond offer may attract demand -- bankers.
newsitem.headline: Turkish fx bond offer may attract demand -- bankers.

text.p: Turkey's newly offered three-year foreign currency denominated bonds may attract demand from banks, bankers said on Wednesday.

"Right now, there is no secondary market for these papers. So we will have to put them aside if we buy. But their terms are good and they may draw some interest," a bank treasurer said, adding that his bank may buy $50 million worth of the bonds.
Earlier this week, the treasury asked Turkish banks to submit their bids for bonds by Friday's close.
The bonds have a maturity of three years with a put option at the end of the second year. They carry interest of LIBOR plus 260 basis points.
Bankers estimate total demand for the papers at between $750 million and $1 billion.
A minimum participation of $15 million in the deal is required and $150 million is the maximum.

"If you don't want to exercise the put option, the return will be LIBOR over 211 basis points," said a senior official of a private bank. "I think the majority of bond holders will tend to hold these papers for three years."
The government aims to extend the maturities and relieve the burden of heavy domestic borrowing by issuing foreign currency paper.

"No-one converts their Turkish liras into foreign currencies to buy these papers. But those who are liquid in foreign currency will buy these papers," said the banker, who declined to be named. "There is liquidity of this sort of around $2 billion in the market."
He said his bank was planning to buy around $70 million worth of bonds.
Bankers say the pricing of the new bonds is compatible with the prices of Turkey's outstanding Eurobonds traded in international markets.
"We can use these papers for legal requirements and as collateral. This increases their attractiveness," the senior banker said. -- Servet Yildirim, Ankara newsroom +90-312-446 2940.
